subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

judge.implied_focus: Expense processing efficiency (how travel-expense records get processed, and their monetary magnitude)

per_column.name: is_processed
per_column.rationale: Binary flag of whether a record has been processed -- a core facet of processing status/efficiency.

per_column.name: days_to_process
per_column.rationale: Processing latency, the central quantitative facet of processing efficiency; also reveals outliers (e.g. 965, 1051 days) worth investigating.

per_column.name: amount_decile
per_column.rationale: Buckets expense magnitude into deciles. Coherent as an analytical dimension, but it centres on spend magnitude rather than processing, so it pulls slightly away from the processing-efficiency focus.

judge.rationale: Two of the three added columns (is_processed, days_to_process) cohere tightly around a single, data-inferable focus: expense processing efficiency/latency, which is genuinely actionable (identify unprocessed items and extreme-latency outliers). These are not mere restatements -- days_to_process derives a meaningful metric from processed_date/opened_at and surfaces investigable anomalies. However, amount_decile introduces a second, distinct concept (spend magnitude) that is not obviously part of the same processing focus, making the set read partly as a small grab-bag rather than a unified facet decomposition around one focus. Structure is sound but thin (only a couple of coherent facets plus a stray dimension), and the deciles column is a mechanical binning rather than a targeted facet. Actionability is solid for the processing angle but diluted by the mixed framing.
